title: Focus day 22-05-24 - GitHub part 2
content:
Attendees:

Agenda:

Sharing and collaboration using reusable workflows and custom actions.

How to start using reusable workflows with GitHub Actions | The GitHub Blog

Creating Custom Github Actions is Easy! | Dor Shinar

demonstrated workflow for updating dependencies. Previous action has now been wrapped in a custom workflow that extends functionality to include even pushing verified build to main if that is wanted.

Discussion around when to use composite action and when to use workflows was concluded as fairly obvious. Differences as well described here, How to start using reusable workflows with GitHub Actions | The GitHub Blog

Key differences between reusable workflows and composite actions

Reusable workflows

Composite actions

Cannot call another reusable workflow

Can be nested to have up to 10 composite actions in one workflow

Can use secrets

Cannot use secrets

Can use if: conditionals

Cannot use if: conditionals

Can be stored as normal YAML files in your project

Requires individual folders for each composite action

Can use multiple jobs

Cannot use multiple jobs

Each step is logged in real-time

Logged as one step even if it contains multiple steps

After discussion around how to best share we concluded that we will create one repository for discoverability. Each logical component would then resided in a separate repository for versioning. As an example of logical component the package dependency workflow meant to be used depends on a custom action in the same repository.

Collaboration would be done as previously using codeowners, PR template and branch protection and IPEX team as contributors.

We’ll aim for focus day with Core team regarding default app etc.
